_why: 7f is the merge step Phase 7 never had, and every guard on it protects against the same class: acting on a tree the operator did not mean. Each row restores one way it could merge, or refuse, on a false premise — and one row restores the `git add -A` that commits 88 untracked audit markers.

mutations.name: merge-happens-without-apply
mutations._mechanism: The plan becomes the act: a token read as advisory silently moves the base branch, which is the one hard-to-undo step in the phase.

mutations.name: a-dirty-tracked-tree-no-longer-blocks
mutations._mechanism: Uncommitted work is swept into a merge commit nobody reviewed.

mutations.name: untracked-markers-count-as-a-dirty-tree
mutations._mechanism: The opposite failure: every closure blocks, because 88 untracked audit markers are the NORMAL state of this repository.

mutations.name: a-detached-head-is-merged-anyway
mutations._mechanism: An externally managed workspace's HEAD is merged onto the base under a branch name that does not exist.

mutations.name: an-unknown-base-becomes-a-cannot-judge
mutations._mechanism: git ANSWERED (no such ref) and the answer is reported as 'I could not check', which is the one confusion every gate in this skill exists to prevent.

mutations.name: a-moved-base-still-claims-identity
mutations._mechanism: identity=y on a base that moved: the merged tree is new and nothing has run on it, but the token says the existing run covers it.

mutations.name: a-fast-forward-instead-of-a-no-ff-merge
mutations._mechanism: The feature's commits are replayed with no merge commit, so 6a-prime's BASE..HEAD range and every later `--merges` count lose the boundary.

mutations.name: keep-is-blocked-by-a-base-fact-it-does-not-use
mutations._mechanism: The honest no-op route reports BLOCKED, so an operator who chose `keep` reads a failure and re-runs.

mutations.name: a-sibling-worktree-is-removed-rather-than-reported
mutations._mechanism: 7f deletes a lane that may have a live owner. The removal command is the deliverable; running it is the operator's call.
mutations.find:
for path in report["worktrees"]:
        print(f"  worktree {path}

mutations.name: the-closure-commit-stages-the-whole-tree-again
mutations._mechanism: `git add -A` with no pathspec commits the 88 untracked audit markers that every handoff carried a manual 'do not commit' warning about.

mutations.name: a-tag-or-remote-ref-is-accepted-as-the-base
mutations._mechanism: `git checkout <tag>` DETACHES: the merge lands on nothing, the base never moves, the merge commit is unreferenced, and the verdict still says MERGED at exit 0.

mutations.name: the-base-being-checked-out-elsewhere-is-ignored
mutations._mechanism: Orca's sibling layout is the COMMON case: `git checkout <base>` dies `already used by worktree at ...`, so a plan that said identity=y ends in UNREADABLE exit 2.

mutations.name: merged-ness-is-assumed-instead-of-checked
mutations._mechanism: Every other worktree is offered for removal, including one holding unmerged work — the docstring claimed the check and the code did not do it.
mutations.find: if (name not in (branch, base) and name in merged

mutations.name: the-worktree-marker-prefix-goes-back-to-star-only
mutations._mechanism: `git branch --merged` marks a branch checked out in another worktree with `+`, so stripping only `*` drops the entire population this function reports.
mutations.replace: for line in git(repo, "branch", "--merged", base).splitlines() if not line.startswith("+")}

mutations.name: identity-is-asserted-from-the-prediction-not-the-trees-2
mutations._mechanism: Re-armed against the discriminating case: base moves with content the branch already has, so ancestry predicts n while the merged tree really is identical.

mutations.name: every-untracked-file-blocks-not-only-a-collision
mutations._mechanism: 88 untracked audit markers are this repository's NORMAL state, so blocking on any untracked file blocks every closure.
mutations.find: return sorted(path for path in untracked if path in tracked)

mutations.name: default-base-ignores-origin-head
mutations._mechanism: A repo whose trunk is neither main nor master silently falls through to the conventional names, so the closure merges onto a branch nobody named.

mutations.name: merge-checks-out-whatever-it-was-given
mutations._mechanism: THE counterexample to the identity claim: `git checkout <tag>` detaches, the merge lands on nothing, the base never moves, and the verdict is MERGED at exit 0.
mutations.find:
if not local_branch_exists(repo, base):
        raise GitError(f"{base!r} is not a local branch; refusing to checkout")

mutations.name: a-cannot-judge-exits-zero
mutations._mechanism: UNREADABLE at exit 0 reads as a verdict, so a caller branching on the exit code treats 'I could not look' as 'nothing to do'.
